fact_check_verdict: PASS with caveats. Two independent validators re-fetched the FNSB results PDF (read as images), Alaska's News Source, KUAC, Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public, the UAF News release and the Zenodo record and API. Vote counts rest on the borough's primary PDF (unofficial). The guide PDF (15.6 MB) was too large to fetch, so every guide claim is attributed to UAF's release or Zenodo. Claims were split into single facts after the check. SB 250 and sponsor unverified, not used.

claims.spoken: On October sixth Fairbanks borough voters filled Assembly seats.
requires: The election was October 6th, 2026. Unofficial results only. Never say certified or final.
claims.verbatim: Election Summary Report ... October 6, 2026 ... Unofficial Results

claims.spoken: About one in five borough voters cast a ballot.
requires: 20.95 percent is the PDF's own figure. Say about one in five. Unofficial results only. Never say certified or final. Do not use the PDF grand total 19,923, it double counts city voters.

claims.spoken: Alexis Howell won the closest borough Assembly seat.
requires: Alaska's News Source confirms Howell won the open seat. The counts are from the borough PDF only. Unofficial results only. Never say certified or final. No position is attributed to Howell.

claims.spoken: She won by two hundred seventeen votes, unofficially.
requires: 7,759 minus 7,542 is 217. Say unofficially in the same breath. Do not use pronouns for Howell, none are given.

claims.spoken: Runner up Miguel Ramirez took no position.
requires: Ramirez took no position. Do not use pronouns for Ramirez. Leaders's moratorium support is a paraphrase, never quoted.
claims.verbatim: I can't really say 'yay' or 'nay' because I think there need to be more studies done.

claims.spoken: Ramirez said there need to be more studies.
requires: Reported speech is a paraphrase of the source quote: I can't really say 'yay' or 'nay' because I think there need to be more studies done.
claims.verbatim: there need to be more studies done

claims.spoken: In August the Assembly asked the Legislature in Juneau.
requires: The Assembly adopted its 2027 legislative priorities 6-1 on August 27th, and the request rode inside that package. It is a request, the Assembly can't impose it. KUAC confirms the date. Say request to the Legislature.
claims.verbatim: adopting a set of legislative priorities for 2027

claims.spoken: The request pauses new commercial data centers on public land until standards exist.
requires: Per KUAC, Aug 31st: halt permitting, leasing or building new commercial data centers until standards exist for electrical demand, water use, environmental impacts and air quality, on municipal or state-owned lands. Attribute to KUAC.
claims.verbatim: until standards exist for electrical demand, water use, environmental impacts and air quality

claims.spoken: A data center bill passed the state Senate fourteen to five.
requires: Per Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media. Bill number and sponsor not verified against akleg.gov (403), so don't name them.
claims.verbatim: This year, the Alaska Senate voted 14-5 to pass a data center bill

claims.spoken: The House never took it up.
requires: The article says the House failed to take it up before the end of the legislative session.
claims.verbatim: failed to take it up before the end of the legislative session

claims.spoken: The bill covered power use and decommissioning.
claims.on_screen: DATA CENTER BILL · POWER USE · DECOMMISSIONING
requires: Per the same article the bill would regulate how data centers use electricity from public utilities and require decommissioning plans.
claims.verbatim: regulate how data centers use electricity from public utilities and require decommissioning plans

claims.spoken: A University of Alaska Fairbanks guide called Computing in Place.
requires: Guide public on Zenodo October 6th (v1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23175112, CC BY 4.0). UAF News release dated Oct 14th, ACEP mirror Oct 11th. Say this month, not released October 14th.
claims.verbatim: Computing in Place: A Conversation Guide on Data Centers for Alaskans, by Alaskans

claims.spoken: The guide asks who benefits and who pays.
claims.on_screen: WHO BENEFITS? WHO PAYS? · AS UAF SUMMARIZES
requires: Questions are UAF News's summary of the guide, not verified against the PDF (15.6 MB, too large to fetch). Say the guide asks, per UAF. Never say the guide contains or lacks figures.
claims.verbatim: What computing does Alaska need? What resources should support it? Who should control it? Who benefits and who pays?

claims.spoken: The Navy's research office funded the guide.
claims.on_screen: OFFICE OF NAVAL RESEARCH · PER THE DEPOSIT RECORD
requires: Funder Office of Naval Research, ARCTIC II, award N00014-22-1-2049, per the Zenodo record only. Ignore the UAF page footer USDA NIFA line. Say per the deposit record.
claims.verbatim: Funder: Office of Naval Research; Program: ARCTIC II; Award number: N00014-22-1-2049

claims.spoken: "I don't think that data centers are good for any community."
claims.on_screen: "NOT GOOD FOR ANY COMMUNITY" · NICK LAJINESS
requires: Quote LaJiness exactly, straight quotes. He is the winning incumbent. His general view, not a statement about the moratorium. Source misspells him LaJinness. Spell it LaJiness.
claims.verbatim: I don't think that data centers are good for any community, to be honest with you

claims.spoken: "A small facility supporting a hospital or tribal government, for example, raises different questions from a hyperscale facility serving global customers."
claims.on_screen: "DIFFERENT QUESTIONS" · LEASI VANESSA LEE RAYMOND, ACEP
requires: Attribute to ACEP's Leasi Vanessa Lee Raymond, who leads the project. Verbatim has for example after government and from, not than. Zenodo lists her as Vanessa Raymond, Concordia University, so state no affiliation beyond UAF's wording.
claims.verbatim: A small facility supporting a hospital or tribal government, for example, raises different questions from a hyperscale facility serving global customers.
